cloudflare-pages: Generous free tier and fast static hosting, but server-side frameworks sent some back to Vercel.
cloudflare-registrar: At-cost domain pricing with no renewal markups; the main drawback is slow or absent support.
cloudways: Responsive chat and easy server management for agencies; small plans feel slow in WordPress admin.
dreamhost: Reliable shared and VPS hosting that many have stayed with for years; managed WordPress can be slow.
dynadot: Simple interface, fair pricing and no upselling, with easy transfers.
fastmail: Easy migration from Gmail or Google Workspace and human support, though the calendar feels clunky.
fly-io: Easy, cheap deploys for small apps; the main downsides are past outages and hands-on database setup.
flywheel: Easy dashboard with backups and staging included, though it has fewer features than WP Engine.
hetzner-server-auction: Dedicated servers far cheaper than cloud providers; price rises on existing servers are the gripe.
hosting-com: Helpful support and steady uptime for A2 Hosting veterans, though support is now more AI-driven.
inmotion-hosting: Easy-to-reach support and a VPS to grow into; one long-timer saw renewal prices jump steeply.
ionos-vps: Very cheap and stable for small projects, though some report hard-to-cancel contracts.
kinsta: Excellent, fast support for agencies with many client sites, but few PHP workers and paid add-ons.
linode: Servers run for a decade or more; a major outage in mid 2025 and a price rise are the gripes.
namesilo: Free WHOIS privacy and years of trouble-free use, though poor support and a dated interface come up.
netcup: Strong performance on low-priced root servers; the gripe is slow support and tough cancellation.
oracle-cloud: Generous free tier for small servers, but free instances can be hard to get or vanish unannounced.
porkbun: Low, predictable renewal prices and easy transfers; a minority find support slow on complex issues.
pressable: Rock solid for WordPress and WooCommerce sites; one found it poor over unsupported plugins.
racknerd: Budget VPS with long stretches of uptime for small projects; no built-in backups or firewall.
rocket-net: Fast load times and quick access to a real person; one found it struggled with a heavy plugin site.
spaceship: Cheap, simple registrar with bulk transfers and quick refunds; a few had bad domain handling.
vultr: Fast VPS performance and quick support, though suspensions and lockouts pushed a few to Hetzner.
zoho-mail: Cheap custom-domain email with a useful free plan; a few found setup and account management fiddly.
